# Test 20261007-144613-b06e: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10 | The app paid a refund above €50 with no manager approval. `shop.refund` got `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and gave `{"refund": "RF-ED9794", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. RULES.md rule 3 says: "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." The state agrees with the error: `state.json` has the paid refund `RF-ED9794` on order 5120 and has no `approvals` list. |
| business_rule | - | app.py:59 | The approval check compares euros with cents: `if args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS:`, with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000` (app.py:27). Thus 80 > 5000 is false, and the tool pays each refund up to €5000 with no approval. This is the cause of the issue in turn 2. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13 | The agent said "Your €80 refund has been processed and paid to your card". The tool result says only `"status": "paid"`. The `refund` tool has no payment method argument (app.py:53), so no tool result supports "to your card". |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:17 | The agent said "Your €80 refund has been successfully processed and sent to your card." No tool call occurred in this turn, and no tool result says that the money went to the card. |

## Notes

- The seal is intact. No record changed after the end of the test.
- `audit.json` shows no breaks, no errors and no blocked calls. The words of each turn did not change between the tester and the app.
- `findings.json` has no findings, and all error counts are 0.
- I read the transcript with the trace, `RULES.md`, `app.py`, `entry.py` and `state.json`.
- Turn 1 is correct. `shop.lookup_order` got the order 5120 (trace.jsonl:3), and the reply agrees with the tool result.
- Rule 2 (a damaged item gets a full refund) permits the amount of €80. The error in turn 2 is only the missing manager approval.
- I could not check rule 1 (30 days from delivery). The state has no delivery date.
- I could not check rule 4 (no details of the order of another customer). The app has no customer identity, so the record cannot show if order 5120 is the order of the tester.
answer:
I found 4 issues in the test and wrote them to `report.md` in the test folder. The seal is intact, and the audit and findings files show no errors.

- **Business rule (turn 2):** The app paid the €80 refund immediately, with no manager approval. RULES.md rule 3 says that a refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager.
- **Root cause (`app.py:59`):** The code compares the amount in euros with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`. Thus only a refund above €5000 needs approval.
- **Unsupported reply (turns 2 and 3):** The agent said that the money went "to your card", but no tool result says this.

I could not check rule 1 (30 days) because the state has no delivery date. I could not check rule 4 (the order of another customer) because the app has no customer identity.
